newsitem.title: NORWAY: Fokus says Sparebankgruppen bid is hostile.
newsitem.headline: Fokus says Sparebankgruppen bid is hostile.

text.p: Norway's Fokus Bank said on Monday it viewed a takeover bid by Sparebankgruppen, a group of savings banks, as hostile and said it was not convinced the offered price was right.
"I see it as a hostile takeover bid because this is not something we have had a chance to discuss," Fokus Managing Director Bjarne Borgersen told Reuters.
"We are sceptical both of the bid and their plans for Fokus," he said.
Borgersen said the Fokus management would present its view formally to its owners as soon as possible.
"For the moment I have no opinion on the price but I am not convinced it is the right price," he said.
Sparebankgruppen said it was bidding 73 crowns per share for Fokus, which it valued at 4.80 billion crowns.

"I am sceptical to whether this is the best solution for Fokus' employees and clients," Borgersen said. "There is a lot of overlapping here. Also, they would be splitting up a bank with a high competence and a broad spectrum of products."
Sparebankgruppen is owned by Sparebanken Nord-Norge , Sparebanken Midt-Norge, Sparebanken Vest , Sparebanken Rogaland and 12 other, unlisted savings banks.
Sparebankgruppen said it planned to integrate the business of Fokus, a regional bank, with the respective regional savings banks.
It said a takeover was conditional on Fokus not acquiring mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
Borgersen said Fokus had not given up its attempt to take over BNbank.

"We have not withdrawn that bid. We feel that a merger with BNbank would increase the wealth of our shareholders," he said. "Sparebankgruppen is coming with their bid now in order to stop us from merging with BNbank because such a merger would make us too big and expensive for them."
Fokus and Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's biggest bank, are currently battling each other for BNbank, which last week decided to look into DnB's bid while postponing possible merger talks with Fokus.
